draft.title: The origins of Shinto
card: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan. Indigenous means it began in Japan among the people who lived there, rather than coming from another country.
Its roots lie in ancient Japanese beliefs and practices, including the worship of nature and the honouring of ancestors. These grew over a very long time.
Shinto has no single founder. No one person started it, so it has no founding moment and no one person who set down its teachings.
Shinto was shaped by Japanese life and place, and it has stayed closely tied to Japan and its culture.
draft.remember: Shinto grew out of ancient Japanese beliefs, and no one person founded it.

a.q: Which statement about how Shinto began is correct?
opts: It grew from ancient beliefs in Japan with no one founder
It was founded by a prophet who lived in Japan long ago
It was brought to Japan from China by a religious teacher
It began when Japan's rulers wrote a set of holy teachings
a.why: Shinto developed slowly out of ancient Japanese beliefs, so no single person started it. The option about a prophet is tempting because many religions have a founder, but Shinto does not.
a.clue: Think about whether one person started it.

b.q: Haruto says Shinto is an indigenous religion of Japan. What does indigenous mean here?
opts: It began in Japan among the people living there
It is the only religion that people in Japan follow
It was started by one leader who lived in Japan
It is practised only by people who live in Japan
b.why: Indigenous means the religion began in Japan among its own people. The option about being the only religion is tempting, but the card says nothing of the kind, and where a religion began is a different matter from who follows it.
b.clue: Think about where the religion began.

a.best: It grew from ancient beliefs in Japan with no one founder

b.best: It began in Japan among the people living there
